mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in quarters where FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a flattening industrial production trend (INDPRO) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND INDPRO flat (<0.2% MoM) for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between the trigger and returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO rising >0.5% MoM for three consecutive months) signals improved manufacturing activity and higher corporate earnings potential, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO acceleration is not followed by a statistically significant positive 20-day S&P 500 return (p > 0.05) in at least 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of >300,000 in a single month, accompanied by a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in triggered months, or the effect reverses (positive returns) in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for four consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces GDP growth and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-mo MA by >10% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods of persistent HOUST weakness as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL (CPI) and FEDFUNDS by more than 0.3% month-over-month indicates a dual shock of inflation and policy tightening, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in months where both CPI and FEDFUNDS rise >0.3% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month average by more than 5% for three consecutive months signals reduced household savings and constrained consumption financing, which lowers future demand and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-mo MA by >5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods of persistent RSAFS weakness as defined.
